In 1949, this incessant war has been raging for 35 years and finally a secret archaeological dig has delivered to the Obscura Korps a long sought ancient relic. This artifact is thought to guard an ancient parcel of knowledge. The exact emplacement of one of the four dark cardinal corners of reality is on the verge of being revealed.

A portal leading to hell, this un-sanctified zone is found buried within the secular crypt of a fortress situated in the heart of central Europe. The Reich's 13th Occult Division is there now. They are about to call upon the Cohorts of Chaos to help them force the world into eternal servitude.

Parachuted behind enemy lines, a fistful of men and women are all the Union has left to thwart this peculiar menace. The Unions finest trained commandos armed with technology still in its experimental stages, the glory bound 42nd Alter-Marine Special Forces must now face the most terrible danger to face humanity in recorded history.

Tannhäuser goes beyond the standard package of set of characters, proposing a vast array of customization, allowing players to develop a unique tactic and style of play for their hero. 10 charismatic personalties await them to be groomed for battle, using over 70 magnificently illustrated types of tokens that faithfully depict various weapons, medals, ranks, powers and equipment.

[Rating: 1/10] The theme seems relatively original. The mechanics are well-thought to simulate snipe-around-the-corner combat. However, this game [b]lacks tremendously in the amount of game versatility and replayability[/b]. By default, the 'Germans' are far superior to the 'Union'. In the house map, limited effect of smoke grenades and ranged weapons make the game seem broken. This doesn't even include the ridiculous abilities and strengths of the Germans.  What made me rate this game especially low is that the strategy is the same every time you play. Union throws smoke and snipes with 1 person, Germans lu

[Rating: 1/10] This game is beautiful, with a quality board and actually rather nice, pre-painted miniatures (although such usually look like crap). The movement system is moderately innovative and plays out nice, and other rules like reinforcement works well and keeps gameplay interesting. The theme is cool, seemingly ripped without shame from Hellboy, and has loads of potential for interesting "roleplay" and story-based campaign play. Sadly, despite all this, Tannhäuser doesn't deliver. The scenarios are rather flat, objective-based missions where you have to use a "skill" (rolling a die) to unlock the tar

[Rating: 1/10] [b]**Biggest Disappointment in Gaming - 2007**[/b]  1st person shooter in a board game. Set up for this game is excruciating, and the mechanics(especially the combat system) are just plain counter intuitive. The game seems simple, but quickly bogs down with a myriad of problems.  I hate to say it, but there is too much player power variance in this one. Don't even get me started on the board. They LOS system seemed to be great though, I just wish they would use it with a game that would make me get more excited about it.

[Rating: 1/10] 39th Birthday give from Charlie, The rule book for this game is poorly written after several attenpts to read thru the rules I have given up on this game. Ill try again if the rule book ever gets rewritten

[Rating: 1/10] similar to the shooter based computer game. Interesting mechanic but little demand for this game.

[Rating: 1/10] El peor juego que he tenido la desgracia de jugar. Una completa pérdida de tiempo.

[Rating: 1/10] Very boring dice-rolling game. Good dice result is key, strategy is secondary. This game demands more luck than brain.

[Rating: 2/10] I wrote a review for this game that explains the very low rating. Essentially this game had such promise and great flavor, but it does not translate well at all to game play. The murky board with the unnecessary pathfinding system is a deal-killer, and the gameplay itself is like a deadly Frag with Adventure! dice pools. Very frustrating for $60.

[Rating: 2/10] Basically a first-person-shooter on a board.  Nice models and easy/innovative LOS rules.

[Rating: 2/10] That a game with so appallingly bland a theme could still leave players with a feeling that the gameplay didn't really do it justice is as good a testimony as any to how bad this game is.

[Rating: 2/10] You know I never understood this game to be honest.  I think I would rather play Call of Duty though.

[Rating: 2/10] Opened, played once. Excellent condition. Includes original edition rules and some of the downloadable add-ons.

[Rating: 2/10] I have never come so close to quitting a game during a game night before.   I stayed out of courtesy...but holy crap this was awful.

[Rating: 2/10] Played once in deathmatch mode.  It seemed like a bit of a dice-fest but I hear that DM is really only for learning the game so now I'm keen to try it in another mode.  I think I much prefer Heroscape at the moment so we'll have to see if there's a place in my collection for this or not.

[Rating: 2/10] I got sooooo disappointed with this highly regarded game. It has nice minis. But the theme, being a good idea, feels weak when playing. The rules are overly complex and quite often senseless. There are always a lot of things to do but none of them interesting. I'm not impressed with the pathfinding system either. After all, just a complicated dice fest. Frustrating.

[Rating: 2/10] unplayable ... I'm sorry, but I can't distinguish the colored lines: rather frustrating!
